overview: The Clean Water Act includes a San Francisco Bay restoration program, run by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), that funds projects to clean up and restore the bay. Today the program works mainly through grants to state and local agencies, special districts, and public or nonprofit groups. This bill would let the program also use contracts, agreements between agencies, and other funding methods, and would open it to federal agencies and other public or private organizations. Program money could cover no more than 75 percent of a project's cost, and non-federal recipients would have to pay at least 25 percent from other sources. It would also bar funds from going to any organization based in a "foreign country of concern," a category in federal law that includes countries such as China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, or that has an agreement or partnership with such a country. As of October 22, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say more flexible funding tools and a wider range of partners will help get bay restoration projects done faster, while the cost-share and foreign-country limits protect taxpayer money.
against: Critics say opening the program to private entities and federal agencies could spread limited money more thinly and pull it away from the local groups it was built to support, and the ban on any partnership with a country of concern is broad.
